A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CULNIG study. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained experiments, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-masking experiments across six LLMs, multilingual evaluations, ablations and module-selective fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds threshold sensitivity, instance-level attribution and NormAd-based neuron-selection analyses.

M1.justification: The main CULNIG pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix I adds an experimental NormAd adaptation whose control inputs blank the country name, unlike BLEnD controls that remove question content; this is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: The represented datasets, cultural domains, languages and NLU tasks are retained. NormAd was already evaluated in v1; reusing it for neuron identification and regrouping existing cultures do not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Table 21 adds NormAd-based neuron selection as an evaluated alternative to BLEnD-based selection. Existing comparisons against random neurons, LAPE/CAPE and alternative attribution scores remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce label-stratified NormAd identification/test halves, selection of instances with correct-answer probability above 0.5, and threshold sweeps varying one module threshold while holding the other fixed. The original benchmark and fine-tuning protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 adds combined-mask threshold sensitivity (Appendix C), regional and linguistic group comparisons (F), instance-level neuron diagnostics (H), and NormAd/BLEnD neuron-set intersection, union and difference interventions (I). These substantially expand the investigation of selectivity, representation and dataset dependence.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random-neuron seeds, standard deviations and the same 2,000-sample bootstrap significance procedure. The new analyses introduce no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original benchmark results are retained, but substantial diagnostic results are added. Table 21 reports 7,989 NormAd-selected neurons and a 1,347-neuron overlap with BLEnD selection; Section 4.5 reports positive attribution on 29% of instances for the top culture-general neuron. Threshold and cultural-group results provide further new findings, rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes explicit attention-forward, GLU and gate-neuron formulas supplied in v1. The attribution definitions, Taylor approximation and selection mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about sparse cultural neurons, shallow-to-middle-layer concentration, effects on related cultures and cultural forgetting during selective fine-tuning. Additional analyses support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 adds a substantive interpretation of neurons as encoding cultural concepts rather than general context-switching signals, and argues that knowledge and values can share neurons. Appendix I acknowledges that BLEnD-only selection misses some relevant neurons. v2 also adds hypotheses about CAPE layer locations and qualifications concerning future engineering applications.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement specifies repository scripts, prompts, CRC data and README instructions, while new diagnostic captions identify individual neurons. The code URL, hardware, runtime and original training details were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. and Wu et al. on multilingual representations, plus Meng et al. (2023) and Fang et al. on model editing. These support new mechanistic hypotheses and prospective applications; the overall positioning against activation-based neuron identification remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the architecture explanation, edits wording throughout the main text, inserts Section 4.5 and a reproducibility statement, and updates affiliations and publication headers. The overall narrative and ordering of retained material remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds diagnostic Figures 5 and 28–30 and Tables 13–14, 18–19 and 21, with localized layout changes. Existing figure artwork is retained. New presentation errors include Figure 29b duplicating 29a despite a different caption, and Tables 18–19 labeling culture-specific analyses as culture-general.

improvement.justification: The added threshold and NormAd interventions strengthen validation of neuron selectivity and expose limitations of BLEnD-only identification. Instance-level analyses and clearer reproducibility documentation also improve the paper. These gains are limited by indirect mechanistic inferences and new reporting errors, particularly the captions in Tables 18–19 and duplicated Figure 29b; the original core evidence remains unchanged.
